commits.pr_title: [Core] Release the FlashInfer allreduce workspace (MNNVL or TRT-LLM) with --enable-nccl-comm-suspend
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Part of #59055 (sleep-mode residual memory).

With `--enable-sleep-mode --enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, `CudaCommunicator.suspend()` only suspends pynccl. The FlashInfer MNNVL allreduce workspace (used by the allreduce+RMSNorm fusion and by standalone FlashInfer allreduce) stays resident while asleep. That is 512 MiB/GPU on DeepSeek-V4 TP4 on GB300.

This PR makes `suspend()`/`resume()` also detach and reattach the group's FlashInfer allreduce workspaces. It reuses the existing `checkpoint_prepare_fi_ar_workspaces` / `checkpoint_restore_fi_ar_workspaces` helpers, which wrap FlashInfer's stable-VA checkpoint API:
- `checkpoint_prepare()` unmaps and releases the physical handles.
- `checkpoint_restore()` recreates them at the same virtual addresses, re-exchanges them over the gloo `cpu_group`, and resets the Lamport flags.
- Because the addresses don't change, captured CUDA graphs stay valid.

Details:
- **Idempotence** comes from FlashInfer 0.7.0: `checkpoint_prepare()` returns early when already detached and `checkpoint_restore()` when already mapped, before any barrier. The executor already blocks a double sleep. There is no extra flag, so if a restore fails (e.g. `cuMemCreate` OOM) a retried `wake_up` retries the restore.
- **Order vs. NCCL** doesn't matter, since FlashInfer synchronizes over gloo. Resume runs in reverse order: pynccl first, then FlashInfer.
- **No workspace** (FlashInfer AR unused): the helper finds nothing and the call is a no-op.
- **Workspaces backed by torch symmetric memory** raise `NotImplementedError` in FlashInfer. The helpers skip them per workspace (`skip_unsupported=True`, set only by `suspend()`/`resume()`), so the other workspace is still released, and log once at info level that the workspace stays resident. The CUDA-checkpoint path (`checkpoint_prepare()`/`checkpoint_restore()`) still raises.
- **FlashInfer all2all** managers also expose `checkpoint_prepare/restore`. They are left out of scope because the default all2all backend doesn't use them.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests in `tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py`, with a distinct mock per workspace:
  - `test_cuda_communicator_suspend_detaches_flashinfer_workspaces[mnnvl|symm-mem+mnnvl]`: suspend/resume routing, and a symm-mem workspace next to a normal one (the normal one is still released and restored);
  - `test_cuda_communicator_checkpoint_rejects_symm_mem_workspace`: the CUDA-checkpoint path still raises;
  - `test_cuda_communicator_resume_retries_failed_restore`: a retried resume after a failed restore calls restore again.
- GB300 tests on the `nightly-af7f9488` image with this file overlaid (identical to `d86cf91240` for the touched file).
- Single-node config: DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 + EP, MTP n=1, `--enable-sleep-mode --enable-nccl-comm-suspend`. The log shows `FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=mnnvl`.
- Harness: gated, deterministic batches. It runs 11 rounds of 553 requests (groups 1 to 256, temperature 0) compared bit-exactly: token ids, logprobs and prompt logprobs. Rounds come after a full wake and after a selective wake (`weights`, then `kv_cache`).
- Then 10 level-1 sleep/wake cycles alternating full and selective wake. Each cycle records per-GPU memory while asleep, and bit-exactly checks the first request after wake against the pre-cycle reference.
- 2-node config: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 over 2 nodes, no MTP, same flags.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 18/18 pass (`pytest tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k "flashinfer or symm_mem or restore"`, torch 2.13.0+cu130).
- The GB300 numbers below were measured on the first commit (08b09bf453). The follow-up commit changes only the failure and symm-mem paths; on the MNNVL happy path the same prepare/restore calls run.

Level-1 asleep memory, per GPU (nvidia-smi):

| Config | Without this PR | With this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| V4-Flash TP4, main | 14029 MiB | **13517 MiB** | −512 |
| V4-Flash TP4, stacked with the other sleep PRs of #59055 | 5161 MiB | **4649 MiB** | −512 |
| V4.1-Flash TP8, 2 nodes (all 8 GPUs) | 19885 MiB | **19373 MiB** | −512 |

- **Stability.** Asleep memory is identical across all 10 cycles with no drift, and awake memory is unchanged. There are no errors or tracebacks, and host MemAvailable is flat.
- **Bit-exactness, single node.** All 553/553 requests are bit-identical in every round, after both full and selective wake, both with and without this PR. The first request after every wake matches exactly in 10/10 cycles; that request is the one that exercises the Lamport flag reset.
- **Bit-exactness, 2 nodes.** Upstream V4.1 TP8 is already not bit-reproducible between two *awake* rounds: 84.1% of requests are identical, and some prompt-logprob NaN 400s occur. Both runs show exactly the same 84.1% in every round, before and after sleep, so this PR causes no regression there.
- **Wake latency.** The mean full `wake_up` goes from 1.58 s to 1.64 s on TP4, and from 1.06 s to 1.09 s on TP8 2-node. The cost is re-creating the fabric handles plus a gloo exchange and barrier. Sleep latency is unchanged.

---
AI assistance: this change and its GB300 validation were produced with Claude Code under the author's direction.

### AMD MI355X (ROCm)

ROCm also uses `CudaCommunicator`, so the new calls run there, but they are a no-op: FlashInfer allreduce is unavailable and a probe on every worker found 0 workspaces. Verified on DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP2 / TP2 eager / DP2 with `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`: memory while asleep matches unpatched within ±20 MiB, outputs are bit-identical after full and selective wake, wake latency is unchanged (0.37–0.42 s), with no errors. Separately, RCCL's comm suspend frees ~0 MiB by default because RCCL does not allocate with cuMem (with `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` it frees 505 MiB, but cuMem adds 389 MiB).

### Re-check on current main, GB300 (single-node groups now use the TRT-LLM workspace)

- Rechecked on main bdd31c31de (clean rebase), GB300, arm64 nightly 18f8f9602 + this PR's 2 files (sha256-gated bind mounts), `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`, 3 level-1 cycles:
  - Since #56891, single-node groups use the TRT-LLM workspace and multi-node groups use MNNVL. This PR frees whichever workspace the group has (both implement `checkpoint_prepare/restore` on FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1).

  | Model | Allreduce workspace | Asleep MiB/GPU without → with this PR | Probes after each wake |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4, MTP 1 | TRT-LLM (default) | −1030 (the TRT-LLM workspace; measured with the graph pool released, see note) | 28/28 ×3 |
  | DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4, MTP 1 | MNNVL (forced) | 9199 → 9139 (−60) | 28/28 ×3 |
  | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 over 2 nodes | MNNVL (default) | 4811 → 4299 (−512) | 28/28 ×3 |

  - Wake time is unchanged within launch noise (V4-Flash ~2.0 s, V4.1 ~1.5 s).
- Unit tests on GB300 (aarch64, CUDA 13.0), rebased on main `bdd31c31d`, run the CI way: `tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py` 39/39 in 3/3 runs, including the 4 new workspace tests (main: 35/35). With #59939 also applied, the two suspend/resume calls compose (46/46 in 3/3 runs).
- Note on the TP4 TRT-LLM row: an earlier reading of 10169 → 8687 (−1482) kept the CUDA graph pool resident, whose size varies by ±452 MiB between launches with the FlashInfer MoE tactic. With the pool released, this PR frees 1030 MiB/GPU at TP4 (the TRT-LLM workspace).

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode layer for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Opt-in (`VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`, meant as the one switch for every model's mono decode kernels) fast path for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode on MI355X (gfx950). Every backbone layer of a decode step runs on persistent FlyDSL launches:

| Launch | Layers | Stages |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | 30 standard layers | the mHC attention seam, then the attention front: wqkv, q/kv norms, the KV insert, wq_b |
| K2 | 30 standard layers | the attention back (split attention, combine, wo_a, wo_b), the attention TP all-reduce, the FFN seam, the MoE (router, top-6, shared expert, MXFP4 experts) and its TP all-reduce |
| FFN | the other 10 | after vLLM's attention seam and attention: the attention TP all-reduce (wo_b's unreduced output pushed to every rank), then K2's FFN seam and MoE |

All TP all-reduces run in-kernel over symmetric peer memory. K1 + K2 replace the ~40 kernels this path launches per standard layer today; the FFN launch replaces the attention all-reduce, the FFN seam and the MoE's kernels on the others.

**Scope**
- **Layers:** K1 + K2 on the 30 backbone layers with the standard mHC seam and no compressor or indexer of their own: 3–7, 9–13, 15–19, 21–23, 25–27, 29–31, 33–35, 37–39. The FFN launch on the other 10: layer 0 (embedding-broadcast seam), the Engram layer 1, and the compressor/indexer layers 2, 8, 14 (also Engram), 20, 24, 28, 32, 36.
- **Steps:** decode only, ≤ 48 rows (8 requests × 1 + 5 DSpark drafts), TP2 or TP4, eager or a FULL CUDA graph. K1 + K2 also need causal SWA windows and `fp8_ds_mla` KV records.
- **Everything else** runs as before: the DSpark draft layers, and prefill, mixed or larger steps. The paths take and return the same tensors at the layer boundary, so they interleave freely.

### Layout

```
vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono_decode.py   eligibility per layer / per step, vLLM tensors -> kernel inputs
vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono/
    runner.py     DSV41MonoLayer: scratch, epoch, peer memory, the launches
    layer.py      K1 / K2 and the FFN launch, composed from the stages below
    attention/    attention stages
    stages/       seam.py (mHC seams, attention reduce), moe.py, moe_shape.py, moe_plan.py, router.py, gemv.py, dims.py
    common/       tagged mailbox, device ops, MX helpers, build keys, peer memory
```

`stages/` and `common/` are adapted from ROCm/ATOM's DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode (MIT License, commit 97359d6). Each adapted file names its origin and keeps AMD's copyright notice. The changes from ATOM:
- the seams are specialized to these layers;
- vLLM's numerics: f32 router logits, the shared expert reading vLLM's row-major FP8 weights, vLLM's `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` and `silu_and_mul_with_clamp`;
- hand-offs carry epoch tags instead of per-step mailbox clears, so no host step hook and the launches are graph-safe. ATOM's clears also wiped what another step width had laid out differently; without them each width gets a scratch of its own;
- ATOM's engine-side modules are dropped.

### Design

- **Weights** are read in place, with no second copy. The attention linears stay vLLM's row-major MXFP8 (32×32 E8M0 scales). The routed experts stay in AITER's shuffled MXFP4 layout.
- **Path selection.** The model is not torch.compiled, so the per-step decision is plain Python. It runs when a FULL graph is captured (uniform decode) and on every eager step. PIECEWISE (breakable) captures are always declined, because they are replayed for mixed batches.
- **wo_b's reduce on the FFN-launch layers.** Their `wo_b` is built with `reduce_results=False`, as the sequence-parallel path already does. A decode step hands the partial to the FFN launch; any other step reduces it in the decoder layer with the same `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`. ROCm's preshuffled-FP8 `wo_b` path now honors `reduce_results` as the linear does. This also fixes a bug on main: with sequence parallelism and an FP8-block checkpoint, `wo_b` was all-reduced and then reduce-scattered.
- **TP ranks stay in lockstep.** Every rank must take the same path at every layer, since the kernels wait on each other's pushes. The conditions read only metadata that all ranks hold alike.
- **Failure modes.** An explicit opt-in that cannot run raises: a CDNA version outside the kernels' (`get_cdna_version()` in `CDNA_VERSIONS`, CDNA4 / gfx950 today, so a later generation is one entry once ported), TP other than 2 or 4, FlyDSL missing, expert / data parallelism or EPLB, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_A4W4_DSV4`, a routed-expert backend other than `AITER_MXFP4_BF16`, or fewer than 256 compute units (a partitioned GPU: every CTA of a launch must stay resident). The MoE and shared-expert tensors are checked for the kernels' shapes and dtypes at the first step, as the attention ones are. A layer outside the kernels' scope is logged once.
- **All-reduces are exact:** fp32 sum in rank order, then bf16. At ≤ 48 rows vLLM's own decode all-reduces are below the INT4 quick-reduce threshold, so the current path runs them exact too.
- **A scratch per step width.** Hand-offs between CTAs are tagged mailbox pairs in a scratch laid out per step width. Each width has its own scratch, allocated at its first (eager) step: 3–16 MB, and at most 8 widths under DSpark. So a word one width polls as a tag only ever holds tags. The MoE's task counters outlive a width and live in the epoch buffer.
- **Dependencies:** the `flydsl` wheel, plus two small AITER helpers that path already depends on: `aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.buffer_ops` (FlyDSL's wheel no longer ships it) and `UncachedIpcHeap` for peer memory.

## Duplicate check

- No open PR targets DeepSeek-V4.1 mono decode. Searched "dsv41 mono", "DeepSeek V4.1 mono", "mono decode layer" and "dsv41_mono".
- The sibling mono-decode PRs are for other models: #59705 (MiniMax-M3) and #60216 (GLM-5).
- This PR hooks per decoder layer rather than replacing the model forward, because only 30 of DSv4.1's 40 layers are eligible.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` (CPU, wired into the MI355 Basic Models job): a decode step takes the mono path and hands the kernels `[blocks, block, 584]` cache views. A padded FULL-graph step takes it too (the kernels skip pad rows, whose slot is -1). PIECEWISE steps, prefill or mixed steps, more decode tokens than rows, non-causal windows, missing metadata, more than 48 rows and the first layer all take the original path. Deployments the kernels cannot run raise.
- `pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` (4 × MI355, its own CI step). One layer with random weights in the checkpoint's formats, at TP2 and TP4: the kernels against the ops vLLM runs for the same decode step (the mHC seams, the ROCm attention chain, the all-reduce, `DeepseekV4MoE`). Each stage is checked on its own input, by cosine and relative error, for the whole layer and the FFN launch, at 1×6 and 8×6 rows. Then both widths' launches are captured in one graph and replayed 300 times, bit for bit against the first run.
- `pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` (same CI step). A five-layer DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP2 and TP4 holding both layer kinds the mono path takes: the whole layer at a ratio-2 and a ratio-1 consumer, and the FFN launch at the sliding-window and KV / index-source layers. It is served with mono on and off on the same random weights, and every decoder layer's outputs at every decode token must match. It runs `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer.forward` as the engine does, so a change to the layer that the kernels do not follow fails it.
- Race stress: the whole layer and the FFN launch in one HIP graph, 48-row and 6-row steps alternating, every intermediate compared bit for bit with the first run. 100K replays each on layers 3 and 9 (ratio 2) and 21 (ratio 1).
- Compile-only build (`COMPILE_ONLY=1`) of the in-tree kernels: K1 and K2 at TP2 and TP4, M = 6 and 48, both layer types.
- No regression of K1 + K2: K2's FFN half is factored out and shared with the FFN launch. K2 disassembles instruction-identical to the first commit's (TP2 M=6 ratio 1, TP4 M=48 ratio 2), and the whole-layer accuracy check reproduces its earlier numbers exactly.
- FFN launch, kernel level: against vLLM's FFN half (the attention all-reduce, `MHCPreDelayedOp`, `DeepseekV4MoE` with its all-reduce) on the real weights of the 10 layers, with the attention partial from a real ROCm attention chain. 48 points: TP2/TP4 × concurrency 1/2/4/8 × 1–6 tokens per request; the 10 layers chained in one HIP graph, cold weights.
- Kernel level (MI355X): the layer against vLLM's own modules (`DeepseekV4MoE`, the mHC seams, the ROCm attention chain, the all-reduce) in a TP process group, with real checkpoint weights. 96 points: TP2/TP4 × concurrency 1–8 × 1–6 tokens per request × the two layer types. Timing: 8 layers chained in one HIP graph, cold weights, vLLM's path captured under `graph_capture`.
- GSM8K: InferenceX's task, 5-shot, full 1,319, temperature 0, concurrency 8, DSpark block rejection; TP2 for K1 + K2 alone, TP2 and TP4 with the FFN launch.
- AgentX e2e with the InferenceX#3690 recipe (this tree's image, a8w4 MoE, INT4 quick reduce), golden DSpark acceptance 3.51, 3600 s per point, c1/c2/c4/c8 at TP2 and TP4.
- Accuracy, per RFC #59665: GPQA-Diamond and AIME25 at TP2, thinking on with `reasoning_effort` high, 8 requests in flight a server (every decode step within 48 rows), against the same build with `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=0`. Long context: RULER NIAH (single, multikey 2 and 3) at 32K, 128K and 256K.

## Test Result

**Unit:** 33 passed. **Compile-only:** all K1 / K2 / FFN builds compile.

**Numerics test (GPU):** passed at TP2 and TP4: every token's output cosine ≥ 0.9993 against vLLM's chain, relative errors 0.3–0.5% (bounds 1–1.5%; a routed scale off by 3% fails), 300 replays bit-exact. **Race stress:** no mismatch in 100K replays on each layer. Before the per-width scratch, layer 3 diverged at replay 13 on every run. **Model-level test:** passed at TP2 and TP4 (9 of 9 local runs of the final version; 40 of 41 of the TP2-only one before it, the failure not recurring and its log not kept). A routed scale off by 3% fails it at both sizes.

**Accuracy**, TP2, per RFC #59665 ([details](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60397#issuecomment-6051909168)):
- pass@1, against this build with `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=0`;
- thinking on, `reasoning_effort` high, temperature 0.6, 8 requests in flight a server;
- ± is the standard error across questions; Δ is paired by question.

| | Reference | Mono |

| AIME25 (16 samples a problem) | 99.4 ± 0.3 | 98.3 ± 0.8 (Δ −1.0 ± 0.7) |

RULER NIAH, long context ([details](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60397#issuecomment-6052301592)): single, multikey 2 and multikey 3 at 32K, 128K and 256K, 40 samples a cell. Every cell is 40/40 for both mono and the reference.


**FFN launch, kernel level, µs per layer** (vLLM's FFN half → the FFN launch, at 6 tokens per request). Every point is faster or at parity: TP2 1.01–2.14×, TP4 1.12–2.32×. The residual and the MoE input match vLLM's bit for bit at every point; the layer output's cosine is ≥ 0.99999, and every token's ≥ 0.9999.

commits.pr_title: [Feat][Frontend] structured decisions: DiffusionGemma read strategy
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Implement DiffusionGemma's structured read strategy for single questions.  Follow-up to #59299.

#60696 (noul and score question types) is landing in parallel. A merge of the two is here: https://github.com/mmastrac/vllm/tree/systemone-question-types-dgemma

## Claims

Serve DiffusionGemma (`DiffusionGemmaForBlockDiffusion`) on `/v1/systemone`.

_Important_: Questions are not diffused en-banc - that will be a follow-up, opt-in option. In this PR, each question gets its own canvas.

- Each question is one read-only request with one denoising step (`diffusion_max_steps` 1, `diffusion_read_only`). The prompt is the same one the next-token strategy builds (A to Z labels, thinking off), ended with the empty thought block a reply with thinking off starts with.
- The canvas is 16 tokens: the label slot as noise, then `<turn|>`, then padding. The label logprobs come from the slot, at the denoising schedule's temperature 1.
(`label_mass` 0.27 to 0.82). With the block in the prompt, `label_mass` at the slot is 0.99 to 1.00.
- The noise at the slot is drawn from a hash of the prompt, so a repeated read gets the same canvas. The DiffusionGemma engine does not guarantee the same output across batch sizes, so reads can still differ slightly between runs.

Important note: The empty thought block must go in the prompt, not as fixed tokens in the canvas. DiffusionGemma fails to converge with the label in the correct slot otherwise.

## Validation

On a GB10 (DGX Spark) with DiffusionGemma NVFP4 (served canvas 64), `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` at 92044241a with this branch's files mounted over it, no additional flags beyond what was needed for diffusiongemma:

- **Question sets**: every answer is right on copy, routing, yes/no and language questions, with `label_mass` 0.99 to 1.00. A forced one-option coin flip reads 0.72. A read takes about 100 ms. Thinking on returns 400.
- **JevBench** (231 public items, one read per item, thinking off, the `jevbench_systemone.py` client from #59299): Intelligence 78.4 to 80.1 over four runs (comparison: djev's published one-step reads score 78.9)
- **Tests**: `test_canvas_read` pins the canvas layout and the thought block appended to the prompt. `pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring` passes on Qwen3-0.6B (41 passed).

## Details

- `NextTokenStrategy` gains two hooks, `_sampling_params` and `_read_input`, which `CanvasStrategy` overrides. `READ_STRATEGIES` maps each supported architecture to its strategy.
- `/v1/systemone` now answers on any DiffusionGemma server. A served canvas shorter than 16 tokens, or a tokenizer without a pad token, turns the endpoint off (501).
- Not covered in CI: there is no DiffusionGemma end-to-end test

## Overview

Makes `test_batched_matches_reference_fuzz` tolerate a one-step fp8 rounding difference on K bytes. Seed 9 fails on the ROCm 10.0 (TheRock) stack (#58761) and in main's scheduled ROCm 10 AMD CI lane.

TheRock's torch GPU `randn` differs from the 7.2 build by one ULP for about 16% of values. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Save the EAGLE attention proof with hybrid Mamba partial tails
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This is the Mooncake connector part of #59826 by @wzhao18. It was split off at review so the core fixes could land first as #60533, which is now merged. The Mooncake store tail save now includes the full-attention KV that proves the Mamba checkpoint under EAGLE. It also pins those blocks until the asynchronous save completes.

## Claims

- After a GPU prefix-cache reset, a hybrid attention + Mamba prompt that uses EAGLE can hit its Mamba checkpoint again from the Mooncake store. Before this change the external hit was 0 tokens.
- The tail's attention blocks stay referenced until every rank finishes the save. They can no longer be reused while the save reads them.
- The scheduler computes each tail once and sends it to the worker, so the blocks it pins are exactly the blocks the worker puts. Later saves no longer re-send the tail.
- The Kimi K3 prefix-cache test starts a Mooncake master from a pytest fixture and runs a Mooncake resend case (`test_mooncake_resend_reuses_prompt_checkpoint`).

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU):

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py
```

| Code under test | Result |
|---|---|
| This branch | 480 passed |
| `main`, with this PR's test files copied in (measured at 22948c5, before the scheduler-side tail commit) | 29 failed, 233 passed (scheduler, worker and HMA end-to-end suites) |

On `main`, failing tests include `test_eagle_attention_proof_published_after_checkpoint_handoff`, `test_mooncake_lookup_reuses_resolved_hash_checkpoint`, `test_finished_partial_tail_is_pre_pinned_as_store_job` and `test_sub_block_partial_tail_offload_reads_cow_block`.

`ruff` is clean. `mypy` reports no new errors: the 10 in `worker.py` also appear on `main` in the same environment and come from pyzmq typing.

**Not run here:** the Kimi K3 end-to-end case (`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py::test_mooncake_resend_reuses_prompt_checkpoint`). It needs GPUs, RDMA and `mooncake_master`; its fixture starts the master, and it skips where the binary is missing. #59826 reports an end-to-end gain with this change and the core fixes combined: Kimi K3, 1P1D DCP8 + DCP8, DSpark k4, prefix-match unit 128. At concurrency 128, the prefix hit rate went from 90.47% to 94.04% and throughput from 11,371 to 15,754 TPS/GPU. Those numbers include #60533 and have not been re-measured for this PR alone.

## Details

**Root cause.** Take P = 7,449 tokens, prefix-match unit U = 128 and EAGLE block drop on, so the Mamba checkpoint is H = 7,296.

1. The first request computes the prompt. On the GPU, the Mamba state is registered at 7,296 and the attention tail at 7,424, which is H + U.
2. Normal Mooncake saves store attention only up to the last scheduler-block boundary, 7,168. Mamba state is never stored by normal saves.
3. The partial-tail save stores the Mamba state at 7,296. But it clipped attention to the same position (key `hash@7296`), so the proof at `hash@7424` was never stored.
4. After a GPU reset, the Mooncake lookup works like this:
   - Attention matches 7,296, and the EAGLE drop brings it to 7,168.
   - Mamba has no state at or below 7,168.
   - The hit is 0.

**Fix.**
- **Boundary puts.** `ReqMeta.boundary_puts` lists every block the job stores under an explicit prefix hash, as `BoundaryPut(group_id, block_id, num_tokens)`. The scheduler resolves and pins all of them; the worker writes each block under `block_hashes[num_tokens // U - 1]` (`_boundary_puts`). Two kinds of entries:
  - **Mamba state.** Each core hand-off, whether a block-aligned snapshot or the sub-block tail at H, becomes one put of the handed-off block. Under DCP, Mamba blocks are smaller than the LCM, and only the boundary block is stored.
  - **Non-Mamba tail.** `_partial_tail_non_mamba_puts` (scheduler, once per store job) covers each non-Mamba group from the last scheduler-block boundary to H plus that group's `eagle_proof_margin`, once that much has been computed. Each block is keyed at its end, clipped to that point; null and missing blocks are skipped.
- **Publishing.** The tail is published on the save that first covers the whole prompt (`ReqMeta.publish_partial_tail`, which mirrors the tracker's `partial_tail_sent`), or when a Mamba hand-off arrives. The boundary is derived from the prompt length, so a job without a Mamba hand-off can still publish the attention proof. Later saves carry no tail.
- **Pinning.** A store job pins exactly its boundary puts' blocks (plus every non-Mamba block for a normal save). Before, a finish-time tail pinned only the Mamba block while the worker read attention blocks from the freed table.
- **Prompt length vs. prefill end.** `ReqMeta` separates `num_prompt_tokens` (used for the checkpoint) from `prefill_end_tokens` (includes output tokens replayed after preemption, used for store masks), and adds `completed_token_len`.
- **External lookup.** It scans past the hit limit for EAGLE groups, as the core lookup does since #60533. The shared helpers `eagle_proof_margin` and `partial_hash_hits_enabled` replace the local copies.
- **Partial hits follow core.** Mooncake used to decide `enable_partial_hash_hits` itself, from the Mamba specs of the groups it transfers. Core also requires every group's manager to support fine-grained lookups (a sliding-window group needs block-aligned ones) and counts groups the store does not transfer, so the two could disagree. Mooncake's scheduler and worker now read core's resolved `kv_cache_config.cache_hit_alignment_tokens`. One core line makes that possible: `engine/core.py` sets the field (and `hash_block_size`) on the scheduler's `KVCacheConfig` as well as the workers'; the scheduler's copy is deep-copied before they are resolved, and core itself does not read them there.

**Known limitations and follow-ups:**
- The prompt-completion tail is sent once. If that save is skipped under store pressure or its put fails, it is not retried; before, every later save rebuilt it (and `batch_is_exist` dropped it once stored). The Mamba state already worked this way, because its CoW block is pinned only for its own job.

**Duplicate check.** #59826 contains these changes. Splitting it into core (#60533) and Mooncake parts was requested at review, so this PR is that Mooncake part, not a duplicate.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used to port #59826's Mooncake changes onto current `main`, run the tests above and draft this description. The submitter has reviewed the changes.

## Overview

## Claims

- Configure the decode split floor per engine through the existing attention configuration API.
- Reserve workspace for the configured floor and pass `min_split_kv` directly to the decode kernel; `1` preserves automatic scheduling.

commits.pr_title: [Core] shm tensor arena for efficient cpu->gpu worker broadcast
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Purpose

`MessageQueue.enqueue` (`shm_broadcast.py`) already routes CPU tensors out-of-band via
`_reduce_tensor` (protocol-5 `PickleBuffer`, #48442), which removed the dominant cost of
the old in-band path — copying tensor bytes into the pickle stream. Two costs remain for
a large multimodal `pixel_values` tensor on a TP=N worker:

1. the out-of-band buffer is published **once per node-local reader** (N transport
   copies for TP=N), and
2. each reader's H2D copies from a **pageable** ZMQ frame (pageable staging +
   first-touch faults).

This PR adds an opt-in **slotted shared-memory tensor arena** that layers *on top of*
`_reduce_tensor`: the writer does **one** memcpy into a free slot, every reader takes a
**zero-copy view** of the *same* slot (no per-reader transport copy), and the mapping is
`cudaHostRegister`-pinned so the H2D is a true DMA. Large contiguous CPU tensors are
diverted by `_ArenaPickler.reducer_override`; anything it declines (too small,
non-contiguous, or arena exhausted) **falls through to `_reduce_tensor` unchanged**.
Net for a ~200 MB image at TP=8: **1 memcpy + 8 pinned DMAs** instead of **8 transport
copies + 8 pageable stagings**. The gain scales with TP degree and tensor size, and is
zero at TP=1 (no multiproc broadcast) — both now confirmed empirically below.

Design doc: `docs/design/shm_tensor_arena.md`.

**Safety / scope:** controlled by the `--enable-shm-tensor-arena` /
`--no-enable-shm-tensor-arena` CLI flag (`ParallelConfig.enable_shm_tensor_arena`,
default on — happy to flip to default-off if preferred); activates only when all queue
readers are node-local; the writer **never blocks** (no free/oversized slot → fall back
to `_reduce_tensor`, deadlock structurally impossible); slot reuse is gated on an
**H2D-completion CUDA event**, so the writer can't overwrite a slot whose async DMA is
still in flight — correct under `--async-scheduling`.

## Test Plan

A/B against **current `main`**: the baseline arm is the unmodified
`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image (`nightly-65b7662d3f…`, includes #48442); the arena arm
is the same image plus this PR's four files. A third arm runs this PR's code with
`--no-enable-shm-tensor-arena` as a disable-control (must be behaviorally identical to
base; also bounds run-to-run noise).

Two setups, so the TP axis and the model-realism axis are both covered:

1. **TP-scaling sweep** — Qwen2.5-VL-3B, TP ∈ {1, 2, 4} (ViT MLP dim caps this family
   at TP≤4), image sizes 512²–3072², 150 prompts @ 2 req/s.
2. **Production-scale VLM** — Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B (ModelOpt NVFP4) on 8×B300,
   TP ∈ {4, 8}, image sizes 1024²/2048²/3072², 120 prompts @ 1 req/s.

Common method: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random-mm` (openai-chat backend), one
image per request at a fixed size per cell, poisson arrivals at a **non-saturated**
rate, 20 warmups (excludes the one-time arena pinning), seed 42, **2 repeats per cell**.
Built-in negative controls: TP=1 (arena structurally inactive) and 512² images (~3 MB
`pixel_values`, below the 8 MB divert threshold).

<details>
<summary>Repro commands</summary>

Server (one per arm × TP; arena arms = same image + this PR's files):

    vllm serve $MODEL --tensor-parallel-size $TP --max-model-len 32768 \
      --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 [--enable-shm-tensor-arena | --no-enable-shm-tensor-arena]

Load (per image size HW, per repeat):

    vllm bench serve --model $MODEL --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
      --dataset-name random-mm --random-mm-bucket-config "{($HW, $HW, 1): 1.0}" \
      --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' \
      --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 64 --ignore-eos \
      --num-warmups 20 --num-prompts 150 --request-rate 2 --seed 42 \
      --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 --save-result

</details>

Still outstanding: port the standalone correctness harness (21 checks: byte-exact
round-trip incl. bf16, zero-copy sharing, slot lifecycle with per-reader release,
event-gated reuse, exhaustion/oversize/non-contiguous fallbacks) into
`tests/distributed/test_shm_broadcast.py` alongside the #48442 tests.

## Test Result

**Qwen3-VL-235B (NVFP4) on 8×B300 — E2E p99, base → arena (mean of 2 repeats):**

| image (`pixel_values` size) | TP=4 | TP=8 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1024² (~23 MB) | 1021 → 995 ms (−2.6%) | 1025 → 999 ms (−2.5%) |
| 2048² (~96 MB) | 1584 → 1298 ms (**−18.1%**) | 1807 → 1363 ms (**−24.6%**) |
| 3072² (~213 MB) | 3340 → 2771 ms (**−17.0%**) | 4132 → 3083 ms (**−25.4%**) |

TTFT p99 moves the same direction (TP=8: −21.5% at 2048², −11.9% at 3072²), and at these
payload sizes TTFT p50 improves too (TP=8/3072²: 1185 → 948 ms). Request throughput is
identical in every cell (rate-limited by design).

  **TP-scaling sweep (Qwen2.5-VL-3B — separate setup from the table above):** TP=1 and
  512² images are neutral (negative controls behave as designed — the arena never
  activates); gains appear only at TP≥2 with ≥8 MB tensors and grow with TP and size. On
  this small model the relative effect is larger than the 235B numbers above — up to −34%
  E2E p99 at 3072²/TP=4 (3020 → 1992 ms) — because the same transport cost is a much
  bigger fraction of a 3B's per-request time, and at 2 req/s its large-image cells carry
  queueing that the stall removal also drains. The 235B table above is the more
  conservative, production-representative measurement. The disable-control arm on this
  setup bounds noise at roughly ±5% per cell.

**Statistical honesty:** with n=2 repeats, individual p99 cells are noisy (the 235B
control shows single-cell swings up to ~±17%). The claim rests on the pattern, not any
one cell: the arena is ahead in **all 12** TTFT/E2E comparisons across both models,
monotonically in TP degree and tensor size — the shape the mechanism predicts
(per-reader transport + pageable staging replaced by one memcpy + pinned DMA), and the
E2E-tail bias matches head-of-line blocking on co-scheduled decodes.

**Summary:** neutral outside the large-image + TP≥2 regime; **~18–25% p99 reduction**
inside it on a production-scale VLM.

**Process note:** the disable-control caught a bug in an earlier revision of this PR —
`--no-enable-shm-tensor-arena` was silently ignored (the gate read
`get_current_vllm_config()` outside its context and fell back to the default). Fixed by
threading the flag explicitly through the executor; the control was re-validated inert
(0 arena activations) before the numbers above.

<details>
<summary>Historical: original measurement vs the pre-#48442 in-band baseline</summary>

Same-seed interactive multimodal workload (uncapped images, TP=4 ×2 workers on one
8-GPU node, ~1.2k aligned requests): TTFT p50 93→89, p90 401→241, p99 1321→862, max
2139→1375 ms; requests >1.5 s: 9→0. These numbers predate #48442 and therefore overstate
the delta vs current main; kept only as provenance for the original problem analysis.

</details>

- [x] Test results — A/B vs current `main` on two models × TP 1–8, with disable-control

## Overview

Makes `test_deepseek_v41_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed` tolerate a one-ulp rounding difference between the fused and unfused TileLang kernels. It fails on MI355 with the ROCm 10.0 (TheRock) stack (#58761) and in main's scheduled ROCm 10 AMD CI lane.

That is legal under hipcc's default `-ffp-contract=fast-honor-pragmas`, and the fused kernel's result is the correctly rounded one. Comparing the reference collapse against the fused residual keeps that check exact without carrying over this rounding difference.

commits.pr_title: [HiSparse] Report host-pool block residency as HiSparse metrics
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With HiSparse and `--kv-cache-metrics`, host-pool block residency (how long evicted prefixes stay recoverable from host) is not observable: since #58725 the host pool has no metrics collector, because sharing the device collector mixed host and device samples through colliding block IDs. Sizing `host_pool_gib` needs this signal.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Accept whitespace around /ci commands and reply instead of going silent
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/ci` comment commands no longer fail silently. Whitespace around a command is accepted, and if a command is unrecognized or the run fails, the bot posts a reply saying so. This came out of [PR 60695](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60695#issuecomment-6090300738), where a `/ci run` got no response at all.

## Claims

- `/ci run\r\n`, ` /ci run `, etc. are parsed as `/ci run`, because `parse_command` now strips surrounding whitespace.
- The workflow now runs for any comment that starts with `/ci` or `/amd-ci`. If the command isn't recognized, the bot reacts 👎 and replies with the list of supported commands. Previously these comments were skipped by the job `if:` without any reply.
- If the job fails (script exception, checkout/uv setup failure, etc.), a final `if: failure()` step comments on the PR with a link to the workflow run.

## Validation

```bash
cd .github/workflows/scripts && uv run --no-project --python 3.12 -m unittest test_run_ci_command
# Ran 56 tests ... OK
```

The new unit tests cover whitespace stripping, detection of command attempts (`/ci rn`, `/CI run` count; `/cifoo`, `/amdci run`, and `please /ci run` don't), the unrecognized-command reply, and idempotency through the existing comment marker. pre-commit passes, including actionlint. The workflow change itself is only exercised once this lands, because `issue_comment` workflows run from the default branch.

## Details

**Root cause (PR 60695):** Dao007forever's comment was created with the body `"/ci run\r\n"` (the GraphQL `userContentEdits` history shows it). The job gate is an exact string match, so run [37999392817](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/37999392817) was `skipped`. Editing the comment to `/ci run` a minute later had no effect, because the workflow only triggers on `created`. Permissions were not the problem: the same user's `/ci run` earlier that day triggered Buildkite #93909.

- I kept the trigger to `created` only. The reply asks people to post a new comment, and an edit to an already-answered comment would be deduplicated by the marker anyway.
- The reply doesn't echo the user's comment back, so arbitrary markdown or @-mentions can't be reflected through the bot.
- Tradeoff: comments starting with `/ci` or `/amd-ci` that aren't valid commands now start a short job on `vllm-runners` and get one bot reply. Comments where the first word is something like `/cifoo` still start the job, but the script exits without replying.
- Overlap check: the only other open PR touching this script is my stale draft [PR 51239](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51239), which covers acknowledgement ordering and deleted comments, not parsing or feedback.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Use int64 index mappings to fix row-offset overflow
commits.pr_body:
Kernels compute row offsets as `req_state_idx * stride`. With int32 idx_mapping / expanded_idx_mapping this wraps once the product crosses 2**31 (e.g. slot 2148 at 1M context, slot 716 for mrope positions), causing illegal memory accesses or silent writes to the wrong row.

Restore int64 for the request-slot index mappings at their creation sites (main and dummy input batches, speculator and dflash buffers, batch-shard local copies, penalties bincount mapping) so the offset math is promoted to int64 in every kernel, rather than casting at each load site. Derived tensors in batch_shard / pcp_manager now use new_empty/new_zeros to inherit dtypes from their source. expanded_local_pos stays int32. The staged-write kernel casts its own int32 row index to int64.

Fixes #57030. Supersedes #60535; the test is adapted from that PR.

Co-authored by @vllmellm.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Trim token_ids/logprobs left past a stop string under speculative decoding
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With `ngram` speculative decoding, a single decode step can accept several tokens at once. When a stop string completes in the middle of that accepted batch, V1 truncates `output_text` to the stop boundary but leaves the tokens generated after the stop in `RequestOutput.outputs[0].token_ids`. When logprobs are requested, those past-stop token logprobs are returned as well.

The root cause is that incremental detokenization appends the whole accepted token batch before stop-string evaluation. The stop-string helper returns a character truncation point, so text gets trimmed but the token ids and per-step logprobs are not mapped back to the stop boundary.

This records the text start offset for each newly accepted token, drops tokens whose text starts after the matched stop string, and propagates the dropped-token count so the per-step `new_token_ids` and `new_logprobs` are trimmed consistently for streaming, non-streaming, and logprobs outputs. It only applies when EngineCore has not already ended the step on a stop token, preserving the existing stop-token termination behavior.

## Test Plan

I ran a real `LLM(...)` reproduction with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `ngram` speculative decoding, `temperature=0`, `stop=[" ha ha ha"]`, and `logprobs=2`. The upstream main check reproduces the leak because the speculative path returns six generated token ids and six logprobs while the non-spec baseline returns three; this branch passes with both paths returning three.

I also ran the focused detokenizer regression file, the existing min-tokens detokenizer file, and scoped pre-commit hooks for the three changed Python files.

## Test Result

The real-engine reproduction shows the baseline/spec mismatch on main and `PASS fixed behavior` on this branch. In the failing main run, both `include_stop_str_in_output` modes return correct text and `finish_reason="stop"`, but the speculative output leaks `[6386, 6386, 6386]` past the stop boundary.

Hardware: one NVIDIA RTX 4090. Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` cached locally at `/root/autodl-tmp/models/Qwen3-0.6B`. import torch

os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS", "1")

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams


PROMPT = "ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha"
STOP = " ha ha ha"


def build_llm(model: str, speculative: bool) -> LLM:
    spec = None
    if speculative:
        spec = {
            "method": "ngram",
            "num_speculative_tokens": 6,
            "prompt_lookup_min": 1,
            "prompt_lookup_max": 4,
        }
    return LLM(

        max_num_batched_tokens=256,

def cleanup_llm(llm: LLM) -> None:

    gc.collect()

def run_case(llm: LLM, include_stop: bool, logprobs: int | None) -> dict:
    params = SamplingParams(
        temperature=0,
        max_tokens=16,
        stop=[STOP],
        include_stop_str_in_output=include_stop,
        skip_special_tokens=False,

    }

def main() -> int:

    matches = all(
        spec_rows[mode]["token_ids"] == baseline_rows[mode]["token_ids"]

            == len(spec_rows[mode]["token_ids"])
            for mode in ("exclude", "include")
        )

    if args.expect == "match" and matches and logprobs_match:

    print(

                "token_ids_match": matches,
                "logprobs_match": logprobs_match,

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support `--stream-interval` and per-request `stream_interval`
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Support `--stream-interval` and the per-request `stream_interval` field (vllm-project/vllm#49754) in the Rust frontend, with the same semantics as the Python frontend's `RequestState.make_request_output()`: the first output is sent immediately, later outputs are merged until they carry at least `stream_interval` new tokens, and the terminal output always flushes. A request's value raises the server-level one.

Builds on vllm-project/vllm#60588 (merged; box rarely-set fields of per-token output types). This replaces vllm-project/vllm#59864 (closed: moved to an upstream branch so it can be stacked) and vllm-project/vllm#50101, which turns `--stream-interval` into a warn-and-ignore no-op.

## Claims

- `vllm-rs serve --stream-interval N` and `"stream_interval": N` on `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, and `/inference/v1/generate` (via the shared sampling params) batch SSE chunks as in Python. `0` is rejected (CLI validation error / HTTP 400).
- No throughput regression in any tested configuration; with `--stream-interval 4`, mock-engine throughput improves by 43–54% over the base PR, with 37–41% less frontend CPU.
- With the default interval of 1, throughput is unchanged to +20% (larger at 32 workers), because the dispatcher no longer clones a channel sender per token.

## Validation

- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vllm-tool-parser-py`: 2049 passed. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
- New tests: `output_channel` delivery batching (first/terminal immediate, multi-token outputs, flush/error ordering), registry abort delivering held-back outputs before the terminal output, `llm` end-to-end merge through a mock engine (`generate_merges_outputs_by_stream_interval`, including logprobs and the request/server interval clamp), DTO/lowering pass-through, and CLI parsing. The existing engine-core client tests consume the stream through `into_outputs`.
- HTTP smoke with the Rust mock engine, 20 output tokens: content chunks are 19 / 6 / 4 for request intervals 1 / 4 / 7 under `--stream-interval 1`, and 5 / 5 / 4 for request intervals 1 / 4 / 7 under `--stream-interval 5` (clamped up, then raised).
- Throughput benchmark: Rust mock engine with DP=4 and `--output-token-chunk-size 1`, Qwen3-0.6B tokenizer, `vllm-bench --backend openai-chat`, random 32→512 tokens, `--ignore-eos`, concurrency 2048, 32768 prompts after a 4096-prompt warmup, GB200 host. Measured at b40ec32a3d against its base ec3c59192b (vllm-project/vllm#60588; its later revision only changes how the terminal chat events hold transfer params), run without `--stream-interval`; all runs completed every request. Two runs per cell, the second round in reverse order; the host had unrelated background load, so differences within ~5% are noise.

  | config | base req/s | i1 | i4 | i16 |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | 32 tokio workers (default cap) | 2801 / 2963 | +20.4% | +42.6% | +63.3% |
  | frontend pinned to 8 cores, 8 workers | 2291 / 2292 | +2.5% | +54.4% | +83.0% |

  Frontend CPU per run vs base: −15% / −41% / −68% (32 workers) and −3% / −37% / −50% (8 cores) for i1 / i4 / i16.

  <details>
  <summary>Earlier full matrix, before stacking (base 5f30fc7031)</summary>

  | config | base req/s | i1 | i2 | i4 | i16 |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | 8 tokio workers | 2930 / 2961 | +1.7% | +18.9% | +61.8% | +55.3% |
  | 32 workers (default cap) | 3019 / 3037 | +12.3% | +6.2% | +45.1% | +52.7% |
  | 64 workers | 2536 / 2599 | +16.1% | +12.6% | +65.2% | +70.3% |
  | frontend pinned to 8 cores, 8 workers | 2114 / 2101 | +7.9% | +18.2% | +46.6% | +71.7% |

  Frontend CPU per run was lower than base in every cell (−3% to −74%). In the last row at i1, steady-state p99 TTFT was 994–1098 ms over 5 base runs and 1044–1080 ms in 3 of 5 PR runs, with the other 2 PR runs (the highest-throughput ones) at 1383/1490 ms; mean and p90 TTFT were unchanged.
  </details>

## Details

**Layering.** The interval rule (first output immediately, then at least `stream_interval` new tokens, terminal output flushes) lives in one place: the per-request output channel in the engine-core client (`engine-core-client/src/client/output_channel.rs`), which groups outputs without merging them. `EngineCoreOutputStream` yields one `EngineCoreStreamDelivery` per group (an enum: `One` keeps the common single output inline, `Many` holds outputs grouped by the interval), and the `llm` layer's `GenerateOutputStream` merges each delivery into one `GenerateOutput` (token ids, logprobs, and sampling-mask rows are concatenated; per-output fields take the later value, as Python does for the flushing output). It still observes request metrics on every raw engine output, so TTFT, ITL, and E2E metrics are unchanged. Merging stays in `llm` rather than the client because the client only sees wire-level outputs (undecoded tensors, opaque values) and metrics need each raw output. The effective interval is `max(request, --stream-interval)` as in Python. It travels in `EngineCoreSamplingParams.stream_interval`, the field Python's `SamplingParams` also carries on the wire (engine-core ignores it; we send the effective value, and omit it when it is 1), and `EngineCoreClient::call` reads it at registration. `EngineCoreOutputStream::into_outputs` flattens the stream for consumers that do not care about grouping.

**Why the engine-core client is involved too.** Merging only in the `llm` layer leaves the per-token cost below it untouched: the output dispatcher, which runs on the dedicated ZMQ runtime, still wakes each request task once per engine step. Those wakes are cross-runtime (`schedule_remote` takes the runtime-wide inject-queue lock). When the woken task only merges and returns `Pending`, HTTP workers mostly idle and park, and the dispatcher convoys on the same lock with their park/unpark traffic. In the same benchmark setup (on an earlier base), `llm`-only batching lost 16–48% throughput at 32/64 workers, and 10% at 8 workers with i16, while CPU also dropped. So the channel coalesces deliveries: the sender holds back outputs after the first until they reach the interval and sends them as one channel message; the terminal output, aborts, `finished_requests`, and client shutdown flush first. The client counts only `new_token_ids` and never merges or reorders outputs.

**Sending under the registry lock.** The stateful sender lives in the registry entry, and the dispatcher sends while holding the registry lock it already takes once per batch. Two alternatives were benchmarked: building sends under the lock and performing them after releasing it, and a per-entry lock. Both regressed at interval 1 (−4% to −25%), most likely from extra per-token work on the single dispatcher thread (sender clone and drop, plus moving each output through an intermediate `Vec`). Sending under the lock was the only placement without a regression in any configuration.

**Other notes.**
- The new request field is accepted by chat/completions/generate HTTP routes. The gRPC `SamplingParams` message is unchanged; gRPC requests use `--stream-interval`.
- Non-streaming requests also merge internally; the collected output is identical.
- `EngineCoreStreamDelivery` is an enum rather than a `SmallVec`: a `SmallVec` channel item added full-size copies per token on the output dispatcher (the serial stage) and cost about 8% throughput with 32 workers at interval 1, while an enum channel item was within noise of the per-output stream (t32 i1/i4 and frontend-on-8-cores i1, two runs each). The `llm` layer matches on it so the single-output case is converted without going through an iterator.
- Moving the dispatcher onto the HTTP runtime would make these wakes local and also lifts interval 1 at 32/64 workers, but costs ~19% throughput when the HTTP runtime is saturated (8 workers on a large host), which is the isolation vllm-project/vllm#46051 introduced. It is out of scope here.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Decode choice specs as JSON in outlines and LMFE
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Choice constraints that contain characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, such as emoji, break the outlines and lm-format-enforcer backends. The choice list is stored with `json.dumps`, which writes such characters as surrogate pairs, and both backends read it back with `ast.literal_eval`, which turns them into lone surrogates. This reads the spec with `json.loads` instead.

## Claims

- outlines: a choice like `["😀 yes", "no"]` now compiles and can be generated. Before, grammar compilation failed with `UnicodeEncodeError: surrogates not allowed` and the request errored.
- lm-format-enforcer: the emoji choice is no longer silently unreachable.
- The default xgrammar backend was not affected and is unchanged.

## Validation

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Reject max_num_scheduled_tokens=0 at config time instead of hanging
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`max_num_scheduled_tokens=0` passed config validation. `LLM.generate()` then hung forever with no error. This PR changes the field's bound from `ge=0` to `ge=1`, so `0` is now rejected when the config is built.

Fixes #60349. The bug was introduced by #44207.

## Claims

- `max_num_scheduled_tokens=0` now raises a pydantic `ValidationError` (a subclass of `ValueError`) at config time, instead of a silent hang. The error names the field and the allowed range.
- `0` is rejected on every user route: `SchedulerConfig`, `EngineArgs`, `EngineArgs` with speculative decoding, and `--max-num-scheduled-tokens` on the CLI.
- `None` (the default), `1` and larger values work as before.
- A new unit test fails on the old bound and passes with the fix.

## Validation

Hardware and software: 1 × NVIDIA B200. vLLM at `43b4aaea3e40e20ef53ce2bfecfa1b72060bf2b5` (before), and the same commit plus this patch (after). Python 3.12, pydantic 2.13. The bug was also reproduced in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit.

Reproducer (`repro.py`):

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
    max_num_scheduled_tokens=0,
)
print(llm.generate(
    ["Hello, my name is"],
    SamplingParams(max_tokens=8),
))
```

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 timeout 600 python3 repro.py; echo "EXIT_CODE=$?"
```

| Tree | Runs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before (venv) | 1 | Engine ready after 158 s. Then `generate()` made no progress for ~362 s until `timeout` killed it. No exception, no error log. `EXIT_CODE=124` | | Before (nightly container, `timeout 180`) | 1 | Same hang. `EXIT_CODE=124` | | After | 2 (one by me, one by a separate review check) | `ValidationError` about 1 s after start. `EXIT_CODE=1` | | After, with `max_num_scheduled_tokens=1` | 1 | Generated 8 tokens (`finish_reason=length`). `EXIT_CODE=0` |

Before:

```
Processed prompts:   0%|          | 0/1 [00:00<?, ?it/s, est. speed input: 0.00 toks/s, output: 0.00 toks/s]
(EngineCore pid=457933) INFO 10-08 07:22:45 [core.py:1423] [shutdown] EngineCore: trigger received signal=SIGTERM
(EngineCore pid=457933) INFO 10-08 07:22:45 [core.py:1581] [shutdown] EngineCore: aborting in-flight requests count=1
EXIT_CODE=124
```

After:

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for SchedulerConfig
max_num_scheduled_tokens
  Input should be greater than or equal to 1 [type=greater_than_equal, input_value=0, input_type=int]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.13/v/greater_than_equal
EXIT_CODE=1
```

Other checks:

- `pytest tests/test_config.py -k scheduler_config`: `2 passed, 439 deselected`. With `ge=0` put back, the new test fails with `Failed: DID NOT RAISE ValidationError`. I ran it with `--noconftest` because my local venv lacks the test dependencies for `tests/conftest.py`. The test is in `tests/test_config.py`, which Buildkite already runs (`.buildkite/test_areas/engine.yaml`).
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/config/scheduler.py tests/test_config.py`: every hook passed or was skipped, including mypy.

<details>
<summary>Config probe on the patched tree (no GPU work)</summary>

```
SchedulerConfig(max_num_scheduled_tokens=0): ValidationError ValueError=True: ... Input should be greater than or equal to 1 [type=greater_than_equal, input_value=0, input_type=int]
SchedulerConfig(max_num_scheduled_tokens=-1): ValidationError ValueError=True: ... Input should be greater than or equal to 1 [type=greater_than_equal, input_value=-1, input_type=int]
SchedulerConfig(max_num_scheduled_tokens=1): OK -> 1
SchedulerConfig(max_num_scheduled_tokens=2048): OK -> 2048
SchedulerConfig(max_num_scheduled_tokens=None): OK -> None
EngineArgs(max_num_scheduled_tokens=0).create_engine_config(): ValidationError ValueError=True: ...
EngineArgs(max_num_scheduled_tokens=1).create_engine_config(): OK -> 1
EngineArgs(max_num_scheduled_tokens=None).create_engine_config(): OK -> None
ngram + max_num_scheduled_tokens=0: ValidationError ValueError=True: ...
ngram + max_num_scheduled_tokens=1: OK -> 1
ngram + max_num_scheduled_tokens=None: OK -> 2048
CLI --max-num-scheduled-tokens 0: ValidationError ValueError=True: ...
CLI --max-num-scheduled-tokens 1: OK -> 1
```

With ngram speculative decoding and `None`, the value still resolves to `max_num_batched_tokens` (2048), as before.

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `SchedulerConfig.max_num_scheduled_tokens` is `Field(default=None, ge=0)`, so `0` passes. The only other check, `<= 0` in `VllmConfig._set_max_num_scheduled_tokens` (`vllm/config/vllm.py`), runs only when speculative decoding is on. `Scheduler.__init__` keeps the value because it `is not None`. So every `schedule()` call starts with `token_budget = 0`. Both scheduling loops (running and waiting) run only `while token_budget > 0`. No token is ever scheduled, the request stays in `waiting`, and nothing raises. A debug run on the old code, with prints added to the scheduler, showed this on every step:

```
LYUTIY-DEBUG Scheduler.__init__ config max_num_scheduled_tokens=0 max_num_batched_tokens=16384 -> self.max_num_scheduled_tokens=0 speculative_config=None
LYUTIY-DEBUG schedule step=1 start_budget=0 end_budget=0 waiting=1 running=0 total_num_scheduled_tokens=0
```

**Where it came from.** Before #44207 (commit `51e0c579b`), the field had no bound and the scheduler used a truthiness test, so `0` quietly fell back to `max_num_batched_tokens`. #44207 added `ge=0` and changed the test to `is not None`. Its goal was to make the non-speculative path reject bad values the same way the speculative path does. But the speculative path rejects `<= 0` ("does not allow any tokens to be scheduled"), while the new bound rejects only `< 0`. This off-by-one turned `0` into a real zero budget.

**Why a bound and not a scheduler change.** The scheduler treats a zero budget as "paused" on purpose, so its behavior is correct. A budget of zero tokens per step can never make progress, on any model or hardware. The sibling fields `max_num_batched_tokens` and `max_num_seqs` already use `ge=1`. The issue asks for a config-time `ValueError`.

**Not done.**

- I did not map `0` back to the default. That would silently replace a value the user set. The documented default is `None`, and the speculative path rejects `0`.
- I kept the speculative-path `<= 0` check. A user value can no longer reach it, but removing it is cleanup outside this fix.

**Limitation.** Setting the field after construction is not validated, because the `@config` dataclass does not validate on assignment. Today only internal code does this (`vllm/config/vllm.py` sets it to `max_num_batched_tokens`, which is `ge=1`), so no user route can reach the scheduler with `0`.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Pin pydantic in the mypy pre-commit hook
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Pin `pydantic` in the mypy pre-commit hook. Unpinned, a fresh hook environment installs pydantic 2.14.0 (released Oct 8) and the hook fails on code that has not changed. First seen on #60721, which edits `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and so invalidated the cached hook environment in CI.

Not a duplicate: no open PR addresses the mypy hook's pydantic version or these `TypeAdapter` errors.

## Claims

- With pydantic 2.14.0 the mypy hook reports 6 `arg-type` errors in `vllm/entrypoints/` (`generate/base/protocol.py:214`, `openai/responses/serving.py:1398`, `launchers/run_batch.py:188,190,197,567`), all `TypeAdapter(A | B)` on a union alias.
- With pydantic 2.13.5 (the version in `requirements/docs.txt`) the hook passes.
- Any PR that changes `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, and `main` itself once the cached hook environment is rebuilt, hits this until pydantic is pinned.

## Validation

Each run used a fresh hook environment and a fresh mypy cache, on current `main`:

```bash
PRE_COMMIT_HOME=$(mktemp -d) MYPY_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) pre-commit run mypy --all-files
```

| Hook environment | Result |
|---|---|
| unpinned (installs pydantic 2.14.0) | Failed, `Found 6 errors in 3 files (checked 2240 source files)` |
| same environment, pydantic downgraded to 2.13.5 | Passed |
| same environment, back to 2.14.0 | Failed, same 6 errors |
| this PR (fresh environment, installs pydantic 2.13.5) | Passed |

## Details

pydantic 2.14.0 changed `TypeAdapter.__init__` to take `type: TypeForm[T]`. mypy 1.20.2 then rejects a union passed there (`expected "type[Never]"`). The call sites are valid at runtime, so this pins the checker's input rather than adding casts or ignores to them.

- The errors only appear in the full-tree scan; running mypy on the three files alone passes even with 2.14.0, so a call-site fix could not be verified file by file.
- Enabling mypy's experimental `TypeForm` feature (`enable_incomplete_feature = ["TypeForm"]`) does not help; the same 6 errors remain.
- The pin can be lifted when the hook's mypy handles `TypeForm`.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Pass reasoning controls through render -> generate
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Mirror https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60062 for the Rust frontend: carry `reasoning_ended` and `reasoning_parser_kwargs` through `/v1/chat/completions/render` → `/inference/v1/generate`, so the engine gates structured outputs the same way as on `/v1/chat/completions`.

## Claims

- `/inference/v1/generate` accepts `reasoning_ended` and `reasoning_parser_kwargs` and forwards them to the engine. Previously both landed in the flattened `other` map and were silently dropped, including when the request came from the Python `/render`.
- `reasoning_parser_kwargs` is typed (`chat_template_kwargs` only), so clients cannot pass arbitrary engine-side parser constructor kwargs: the engine receives only what Rust re-serializes.
- `/v1/chat/completions/render` emits the values the Rust chat route sends to the engine: `reasoning_ended` from the parser-built output grammar and the effective chat template kwargs. Completion render emits neither.

## Validation

From `rust/`:

```sh
cargo nextest run --locked -p vllm-server -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-chat -p vllm-llm -p vllm-text
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
```

1096 tests passed. New and updated coverage:

- `prepare_generate_request_forwards_reasoning_controls`: omitted, `reasoning_ended=false` with kwargs, and `reasoning_ended=true` with empty kwargs lower to the expected `TextRequest` fields.
- `render_chat_response_can_be_submitted_to_generate_unchanged`: the render output carries `chat_template_kwargs`, and the mock engine receives them in `EngineCoreRequest.reasoning_parser_kwargs` after submitting the render output unchanged to generate.
- `render_completion_returns_generate_request_with_body_request_id`: completion render omits both fields.

No real-model validation yet; this is a draft.

## Details

Not duplicating an open PR: the open gRPC counterpart https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59836 changes the gRPC `Generate` API, not the HTTP route.

- The route reuses `ReasoningParserKwargs`, the engine-core protocol type that is already the `TextRequest` field type, adding only a serde default for `chat_template_kwargs` so `{}` is accepted like Python's `default_factory=dict`. Unknown keys are ignored rather than rejected, consistent with the rest of this request type (unknown top-level fields go to the ignored `other` map); unlike Python's `model_dump()`, they cannot reach the engine.
- Render omits `reasoning_parser_kwargs` when it equals the default. Generate maps an omitted value to the default, which is what the Rust chat and completion routes send today, so omission is lossless.
- Rust chat does not yet resolve `reasoning_ended=true` for `include_reasoning=false` as Python does; render reproduces whatever the Rust chat route sends, so that gap is unchanged here.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Pass through raw characters in byte-level decode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend's byte-level decode fast path turns raw whitespace in added tokens into NUL bytes. Pass those characters through, as HuggingFace `tokenizers` does.

## Claims

- Non-special added tokens whose content has a raw space, newline, or other character the GPT-2 byte table never emits now decode verbatim instead of as `\0`.
- Fixes code indentation for GPT-NeoX-tokenizer models (Pythia, OLMoE, Mamba), whose whitespace-run added tokens decode to runs of `\0` on `main`.
- Fixes tool-call parsing when the parser's markup is such a token: a checkpoint with `<parameter name="` / `\n</parameter>`-style added tokens returned every tool call with `"arguments": "{}"` from the Rust frontend, while Python parsed them correctly from the same token IDs.

## Validation

```bash
cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-tokenizer
cargo clippy -p vllm-tokenizer --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

- `vllm-tokenizer`: 96 passed. The new `added_tokens_with_raw_whitespace_decode_verbatim` fails on `main` with `left: "<parameter\0name=\"city\">\nParis\0</parameter>…"` and passes here; it checks the fastokens fast path and the HF backend against the same text, including an added token `\ncafé` that a per-character pass-through decodes as `\ncaf�`.
- Real tokenizer, out of tree: a scratch crate with a path dependency on `vllm-tokenizer` decodes `def f(x):\n        if x:\n                return x\n` with `allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct`'s `tokenizer.json` (IDs 50270 and 50262 are 8- and 16-space added tokens):
  - `main`: `"def f(x):\n\0\0\0\0\0\0\0\0if x:\n\0\0\0…\0return x\n"`
  - this PR: identical to the HF backend and the original text.
- End to end, on the checkpoint with tool-call markup tokens (GB200, TP4): prompt and generated token IDs were identical between the Python and Rust frontends, and the Rust raw completion text showed the `\0` in place of the space and newline. That run predates this patch; the unit test reproduces the same decoded string.

## Details

`CHAR_TO_BYTE` is a flat reverse table over U+0000..U+0143, filled only at the 256 codepoints the GPT-2 byte-to-unicode map emits. Every other slot was `0`, so a codepoint like U+0020 or U+000A mapped to byte 0 instead of falling through to the pass-through branch that already handles non-GPT-2 codepoints such as DeepSeek's `｜` and `▁`. Byte-level vocab entries never contain those codepoints, but added tokens store raw text, and `id_to_token` returns that text unchanged. HuggingFace's `ByteLevel` decoder passes a token through verbatim when any of its characters is unmapped, so the Python frontend was unaffected.

The table now stores `Option<u8>`, and a token with any `None` or out-of-table codepoint passes through whole, as in HF. Characters the table does emit in the same token, such as `Ġ` or `é`, therefore stay verbatim; previously, out-of-table codepoints such as DeepSeek's passed through one character at a time. The common path still does one table lookup per character.

The fast path was written to match `fastokens::decoders::ByteLevelDecoder`, and fastokens 0.2.1 has the same table; that will be fixed there separately. vLLM only reaches fastokens' decoder for decoders that are not a single `ByteLevel` stage, so the common byte-level tokenizers are covered by this change.

Duplicate check: no open PR touches `byte_level_decode.rs` or byte-level decoding of added tokens.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Box rarely-set fields of per-token output types
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Box the rarely-set fields of the Rust frontend's per-token output types (`EngineCoreOutput`, `GenerateOutput`, `ChatEvent`, and the internal `AssistantEvent`). These values are moved by value through the output dispatcher, the per-request channel, and the `llm`/`chat` layers once per engine step, so their inline size is paid on every token.

This is the base of a stack; the `--stream-interval` support PR sits on top of it.

## Claims

- `EngineCoreOutput` 648 → 264 bytes (`EngineCoreStreamOutput` 664 → 280), `GenerateOutput` 472 → 168, `ChatEvent` 232 → 104, `AssistantEvent` 208 → 80.
- Mock-engine throughput with 32 tokio workers +18.8%; frontend pinned to 8 cores +4.5%; 8 workers on a large host unchanged.
- No wire or API behavior change: the msgpack format is unchanged (`Box` is transparent to serde), and per-request types keep their unboxed fields.

## Validation

- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vllm-tool-parser-py`: 2039 passed. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass. The existing Python-wire decode test (`tests/client.rs`, Python-encoded `EngineCoreRequest`/outputs) and Debug snapshots are unchanged.
- Type sizes from `cargo +nightly rustc -p vllm-server --lib --release -- -Zprint-type-sizes`, before → after: `EngineCoreOutput` 648 → 264, `EngineCoreStreamOutput` 664 → 280, `GenerateOutput` 472 → 168, `GenerateOutputStream` 520 → 424, `ChatEvent` 232 → 104, `AssistantEvent` 208 → 80.
- Throughput benchmark: Rust mock engine with DP=4 and `--output-token-chunk-size 1`, Qwen3-0.6B tokenizer, `vllm-bench --backend openai-chat`, random 32→512 tokens, `--ignore-eos`, concurrency 2048, 32768 prompts after a 4096-prompt warmup, GB200 host, frontend and mock on cores 0–69, client on 70–139. Measured at ec3c59192b (the later revision only changes how terminal chat events hold transfer params); base is 7d47ac2ddb. Two runs per cell, the second round in reverse order; the host had unrelated background load.

  | config | base req/s | this PR req/s | change |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | 8 tokio workers | 3020 / 2872 | 2912 / 3065 | +0.3% (noise) |
  | 32 tokio workers (default cap) | 2516 / 2468 | 3049 / 2871 | +18.8% |
  | frontend pinned to 8 cores, 8 workers | 2176 / 2211 | 2298 / 2285 | +4.5% |

## Details

**Why.** While implementing `--stream-interval`, a few refactors that only changed how outputs are wrapped (a `SmallVec` channel item, iterator adapters around a delivery) regressed throughput by 7–17%. Disassembly showed one to three extra full-size `memcpy`s of the 664-byte `EngineCoreStreamOutput` per token in the dispatcher and the request task. With 32 workers the single output dispatcher is the bottleneck, so its per-token copy cost turns directly into throughput. Shrinking the moved types makes every copy on this path cheaper and makes the path less sensitive to such wrapping.

**What is boxed.** Only fields that are absent on most outputs:

- `EngineCoreOutput`: `pooling_output` (pooling only), `kv_transfer_params` / `ec_transfer_params` (final output, disaggregated serving), `trace_headers` (tracing), `prefill_stats` (first output), `routed_experts` (opt-in), `spec_decode_metrics` (final output, opt-in), `prompt_token_id_logprobs` (first output, opt-in). Per-step fields (`request_id`, `new_token_ids`, `new_logprobs`, `new_sampling_mask`, `events`, ...) stay inline.
- `GenerateOutput`: `prompt_info` (first output), `kv_transfer_params`, `ec_transfer_params`, `spec_decode_metrics`. The boxes are moved through from the engine output, so no extra allocation per step.
- `ChatEvent::Done` and the internal `AssistantEvent::Done`: `kv_transfer_params`, `ec_transfer_params`, which made every per-token `ChatEvent` 232 bytes and `AssistantEvent` 208 bytes. `text::Finished` carries the same boxes through unchanged, so the streaming path never unboxes and boxes them again.

`serde_json::Value` is 72 bytes here because the workspace enables `preserve_order`, which is why the two transfer-params fields were large in every layer.

**Allocation cost.** A boxed field allocates only when present: `prefill_stats` and `prompt_info` once per request, the rest only when the feature is used. Per-request collected types (`CollectedGenerateOutput`, `CollectedTextOutput`, `CollectedAssistantMessage`) and response DTOs keep unboxed fields and unbox at collection, so downstream code is unchanged.
