commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Treat max_tokens as output upper bound, not input-space reservation
commits.pr_body:
## Why are these changes needed?

Fixes #42474.

`TokenizeParams.max_input_tokens` was defined as `max_total_tokens - max_output_tokens`, treating the client's requested `max_tokens` as a **hard reservation** off the model's context window. Per the OpenAI API spec — and how Zed/Factory/opencode-style clients actually use it — `max_tokens` is an *upper bound* on generation, not a reservation. The real generation budget is already clamped downstream by `get_max_tokens()` in `vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/api_utils.py` based on actual post-tokenization prompt length, so the output side stays bounded regardless.

Example: model context 128000, prompt 62466 tokens, `max_tokens: 65535`
- before: rejected (`62466 > 128000-65535 = 62465`)
- after: prompt accepted, sampling `max_tokens` clamped to `65534`

## Why this is a fix at the source, not whack-a-mole

The property feeds seven consumers. Patching only one (e.g. `_token_len_check` alone) left `get_encode_kwargs` capping the tokenizer at `max_input_tokens + 1`, silently truncating prompts for left-truncation chat models and breaking prefix-cache locality. Fixing the property at the source corrects all seven consistently.

## What stays correct

- `__post_init__` still rejects `max_output_tokens > max_total_tokens` (a genuine bug)
- `_token_len_check` / `_text_len_check` still reject genuine context overflow; their messages are updated to reflect that the rejection means *input alone* exceeds the context, not input+output
- `with_kwargs` now preserves the original `max_output_tokens` when no explicit `max_length` is passed, instead of recomputing it to 0 (this was flagged on the existing POC PR)
- `get_max_tokens()` continues to clamp `sampling_params.max_tokens` to `max_model_len - input_length`

## Tests

`tests/renderers/test_completions.py::TestMaxTokensNotReservation` (7 tests):
- large `max_tokens` no longer eats the prompt budget (the reported symptom)
- genuine prompt overflow is still rejected
- `truncate_prompt_tokens=-1` / `pad_prompt_tokens=-1` map to `max_total_tokens`, not `max_total - max_output`
- `with_kwargs` preserves/re-derives the output budget correctly

All pre-existing renderer tests run with `max_output_tokens=0`, so their behavior is unchanged.

## Related PR

#42482 is an open proof-of-concept for the same fix. This PR additionally addresses the functional regression (output budget reset in `with_kwargs`) and the now-inconsistent validation messages that its bot review called out.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Allow 10% ngram acceptance drop under preemption on CUDA in test_async_scheduling_accuracy
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling_accuracy.py::test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding` compares each spec-decode config's acceptance against the first (no-preemption) config, allowing a 5% relative drop on CUDA. The **preemption** configs sit right at that floor and flip between passing and failing. That happens on `main` too, not only on torch-bump PRs:

| Build | Lane | Acceptance vs baseline | Drop |
|---|---|---|---|
| [92956](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/92956) | `main` (torch 2.13) | 0.0679 vs 0.0727 | 6.6% |
| [93148](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93148) | torch 2.14.1 PR (#52183) | 0.0679 vs 0.0727 | 6.6% |
| [93349](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93349) | torch 2.14.1 PR (#52183) | 0.0705 vs 0.0765 | 7.8% |
| [93464](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93464#01a118e1-24b0-4de4-ae95-0a54dcb719a8) | torch 2.15.0 RC PR (#60324) | 0.0724 vs 0.0765 | 5.3% |

Preemption recomputes requests and loses their n-gram drafts, which is why ROCm already gets a 10% allowance for preemption configs. This applies the same allowance on CUDA. Non-preemption configs keep the 5% floor.

## Test Plan

Test-only change. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the file. Every failing data point above is within the new 10% allowance; the non-preemption assertions are unchanged.

## Test Result

The same change has been carried on the torch 2.14.1 (#52183) and 2.15.0 (#60324) bump PRs. Landing it here removes the flake from `main` and lets both PRs drop their copy.

Tracking: pytorch/test-infra#9075.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Wait for VRAM to settle before building LLM in test_full_graph
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`tests/compile/fullgraph/test_full_graph.py` builds `LLM` directly and so skips the ROCm startup-memory guard that every `VllmRunner`-based test has had since [#49287](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49287). When the device is not free as a test starts, the engine fails its startup check instead of waiting for the memory to come back. Call the same guard `VllmRunner` calls.

Six tests in this file failed that way on the `:amd: (MI355 DPX) PyTorch Fullgraph` step in [Buildkite #93716](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93716/list?jid=01a11edf-b64d-4af0-91f8-60f8f72d7308&tab=output).

## Claims

- The memory was not this job's. `rocm-smi`, run by the step before any test started, shows a PID outside the job's pod holding 43.7 GiB on a card already 89% occupied.
- The threshold is the engine's own condition rather than a tuned constant. Startup requires free memory of at least `total * utilization`, so the wait is for used memory to fall to `total * (1 - utilization)`.
- The wait would have been long enough. The six failures span 103 seconds; usage dropped 147 s after the file started and every later test passed, against a 240 s bound.
- No-op when the device is clean, and no-op off ROCm, so NVIDIA steps are unaffected.

## Validation

1× AMD MI355X (gfx950, 287.98 GiB, SPX), ROCm 7.2, PyTorch `2.13.0+git733fca1`, vLLM `19c0bed584`. The CI condition was reproduced by holding 40 GiB in a separate process and releasing it 90 s later, which puts the device above the 23.04 GiB this card implies at the default utilization of 0.92.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| One test, 40 GiB held, before this change | failed in 11 s on the startup check, 247.31 of 287.98 GiB free against 264.95 needed |
| Same, after this change | waited 78 s for the release, then passed |
| Whole file, clean device | 11 passed, no wait |

The first row is the same failure as the six in CI.

## Details

Converting `run_model` to `VllmRunner` would pick up the guard at both construction and teardown, but `VllmRunner` also overrides `max_model_len`, `block_size`, `enable_chunked_prefill` and `kernel_config.enable_jit_warmup`, all of which change what a compilation test compiles. The teardown half is worth little here anyway, since every test in this file runs in its own process.
